newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Morgan Stanley sees good return on Kazakh Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley sees good return on Kazakh Eurobond.

text.p: Kazakhstan's Eurobond offers attractive returns and the Central Asian republic's sovereign debt could be upgraded, Morgan Stanley said.

Returns on Kazakhstan's 9.25 percent three-year Eurobond maturing December 1999 could range between 9.2 percent and 11.7 percent over the next year, depending on to what extent it is upgraded, it said in a research note by analyst Eric Fine.
"We believe Kazakhstan's Eurobond returns are likely to be attractive, given the country's very strong credit and the potential for ratings upgrades," Morgan Stanley said.
Dollar returns on Kazakh T-bills could be even higher, at 17 percent over the next year, it said.

Morgan Stanley said Kazakhstan was arguably an investment- grade credit, with low debt, small financing needs, high foreign direct investment, a growing export base and improving growth and stabilisation prospects.
"Kazakhstan's current account will in our view improve dramatically over the next several years as the country's natural resource base is increasingly and more effectively exploited," it said.
But Kazakhstan's dependence on Russia for imports, exports, oil export routes and overall political stability is a key risk.
Growth in the economy, which has now bottomed out, should improve, as natural resource output increases, investment flows in and domestic demand picks up, it said.
Strong anti-inflationary monetary and fiscal policies, the continued anti-inflationary potential of the tenge currency and strong capital inflows will continue monetary stabilisation.
The strong constitutional position of President Nursultan Nazarbayev, whose term runs to 2001, the political scene will be stable and government reforms can continue, it said.
